note: Each callback names a source page that supports both scenes or the link between them. Scene locators are plain descriptions, not timestamps. Fact-checked 2026-10-06.

callbacks.title: Proof That Tony Stark Has a Heart

foreshadow.scene: After Tony's new reactor is fitted
foreshadow.description: Pepper has Tony's original arc reactor mounted in a glass case engraved "Proof that Tony Stark has a heart" and gives it to him.

fulfillment.description: At the lakeside funeral, Pepper sets that same engraved reactor on a wreath of flowers and lets it float out onto the water.

callbacks.explanation: The first object that kept Tony alive becomes his memorial. The engraving that started as Pepper's joke in 2008 reads very differently eleven years later.

source.name: Den of Geek: Avengers: Endgame - Who Was in That Important Spoiler Scene

callbacks.title: The Icing Problem

foreshadow.description: Testing his new suit, Tony climbs too high and the armor ices up and stops working, a weakness he learns about the hard way.

fulfillment.description: Tony leads Stane's copied armor high into the sky, where it ices up: the same flaw Tony ran into on his test flight.

callbacks.explanation: The setup and payoff sit in the same film. According to the film's production history, the ending was rewritten late to call back to the freezing flaw because the first cut of the final act was just two robots punching each other.

callbacks.title: Obadiah Stane's Betrayal

foreshadow.description: Obadiah Stane, Howard Stark's old partner who runs the company, warns Tony that quitting weapons will ruin Stark Industries, and keeps asking about Tony's new work.

fulfillment.description: Stane is revealed to have been selling weapons to the Ten Rings and hiring them to kill Tony. He steals the reactor from Tony's chest to power his own armor.

callbacks.explanation: The father figure who seemed to be protecting the company was the one who arranged Tony's capture. Both halves happen inside the first film.

callbacks.title: J.A.R.V.I.S. Flies the Suit

foreshadow.description: J.A.R.V.I.S. debuts as the AI that runs Tony's house and his Iron Man suits.

fulfillment.scene: Escape from Malibu and the oil-rig battle
fulfillment.description: J.A.R.V.I.S. flies the damaged suit, with Tony inside, to Tennessee after the house is destroyed, and later remote-controls dozens of Iron Man suits in the final battle.

callbacks.explanation: The workshop helper from the first film ends up doing the flying himself. By Iron Man 3 the suits can fight with nobody inside them.

callbacks.title: Tony and Pepper

foreshadow.description: Pepper reaches into Tony's chest to swap his arc reactor at his request, and the two grow closer through the film.

fulfillment.description: After Tony saves her from an exploding drone, Pepper and Tony kiss for the first time and admit their feelings.

callbacks.explanation: The first film keeps the romance as subtext. The sequel pays it off. Iron Man 3 then has them living together.

callbacks.title: Yinsen's Sacrifice

foreshadow.description: Yinsen, the doctor who saved Tony's life, runs at the Ten Rings to buy time while the Mark I suit powers up, and dies.

fulfillment.description: Tony takes the Infinity Stones into his own armor and uses them to wipe out Thanos and his army, fatally injuring himself.

callbacks.explanation: Tony's story as Iron Man begins with someone dying so he can live and ends with Tony dying so others can live.

callbacks.title: Ivan Vanko's Revenge

foreshadow.description: Mourning his father Anton, Ivan Vanko watches Tony reveal himself as Iron Man on the news and builds his own arc reactor from his father's old Stark blueprints.

fulfillment.scene: Monaco race and the Stark Expo battle
fulfillment.description: Vanko attacks Tony at the Monaco Grand Prix with electrified whips, then returns at the Expo in armor with an army of drones. Nick Fury explains that Howard Stark had Anton deported for trying to sell the reactor.

callbacks.explanation: The villain is the Stark family's past coming back: the same reactor technology, from the partner Howard pushed out.

callbacks.title: Stark Industries' Weapons Legacy

foreshadow.description: After being wounded by one of his own company's missiles in Afghanistan, Tony announces that Stark Industries will stop making weapons.

fulfillment.description: Tony and Steve find out that S.H.I.E.L.D. plans to use the Tesseract to build weapons, and the team turns on itself.

callbacks.explanation: The man who walked away from making weapons finds his new allies planning to make them.

callbacks.title: The Avengers Initiative

foreshadow.description: Nick Fury visits Tony at home, tells him he has become part of a bigger universe, and says he wants to talk about the "Avenger Initiative".

fulfillment.description: Fury reactivates the Avengers Initiative and brings in Steve Rogers, Bruce Banner and Tony to go after Loki.

callbacks.explanation: This was Samuel L. Jackson's first appearance as Fury. The team he mentions in 2008 finally assembles four years later.

callbacks.title: "I Am Iron Man" Has Consequences

foreshadow.description: Tony drops the cover story he was given and tells the press that he is Iron Man.

fulfillment.description: Ivan Vanko sees the reveal on the news and starts building his own reactor, and Tony is pressed to hand his armor over to the government.

callbacks.explanation: Without a secret identity, Tony's technology and life are public. The sequel is built on the trouble that causes.

callbacks.title: Rhodey's Suit

foreshadow.description: James "Rhodey" Rhodes, an Air Force officer and Tony's best friend, is introduced as Tony's military contact. Director Jon Favreau cast Terrence Howard partly because he could play War Machine in a sequel.

fulfillment.description: Rhodes, now played by Don Cheadle, puts on one of Tony's suits to stop a drunk Tony and takes it to the Air Force. Weaponized, it becomes War Machine.

callbacks.explanation: Planned from the first film: the friend in uniform becomes the second armored hero. His military loyalty is what puts the suit in the government's hands.

callbacks.title: Agent Coulson's First Case

foreshadow.description: Agent Phil Coulson, the first S.H.I.E.L.D. agent seen in the MCU, wants to debrief Tony on his captivity and later helps Pepper go after Obadiah Stane.

fulfillment.description: Coulson is killed by Loki, and Fury uses his death to make the Avengers work together.

callbacks.explanation: A small part in 2008 grew across Iron Man 2 and Thor until his death brought the team together.

callbacks.title: Natalie Rushman Is Natasha Romanoff

foreshadow.description: "Natalie Rushman" becomes Tony's new personal assistant when Pepper becomes CEO. Fury later reveals she is S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Natasha Romanoff.

fulfillment.description: Natasha recruits Bruce Banner, frees Clint Barton from Loki's control and uses Loki's scepter to close the portal over New York.

callbacks.explanation: The undercover spy from Iron Man 2 becomes one of the six founding Avengers.

callbacks.title: The Tesseract Comes Back

foreshadow.scene: Opening at the S.H.I.E.L.D. research base
foreshadow.description: Erik Selvig is studying the Tesseract for S.H.I.E.L.D. when it opens a portal and Loki comes through and steals it.

fulfillment.description: Tony and Scott fail to take the 2012 Tesseract after the Battle of New York, so Tony and Steve travel to 1970 and take it from Camp Lehigh instead.

callbacks.explanation: Endgame goes back to the very case and the very cube from The Avengers. The first attempt fails and the team has to look for it even further back.

callbacks.title: Bruce Banner's Anger

foreshadow.description: After losing control on the Helicarrier, Bruce tells Steve that his secret is that he is "always angry", and becomes the Hulk on purpose.

fulfillment.description: Bruce has merged his mind with the Hulk's body, keeping the Hulk form while staying himself.

callbacks.explanation: In The Avengers Bruce learns to choose when to change. By Endgame the two sides have become one person.

callbacks.title: Clint and Natasha

foreshadow.description: Clint Barton spends most of the film under Loki's mind control until Natasha fights him and frees him.

fulfillment.description: To get the Soul Stone, one of them has to give up their life. Each tries to be the one, and Natasha dies so Clint can bring the Stone back.

callbacks.explanation: In 2012 Natasha saves Clint's mind. In Endgame she saves his life, at the cost of her own.

callbacks.title: Loki and the Tesseract

foreshadow.description: Loki comes to Earth through the Tesseract and steals it. At the end, Thor takes Loki and the Tesseract back to Asgard.

fulfillment.description: When the heist goes wrong, the Tesseract lands at the 2012 Loki's feet. He grabs it and escapes through a portal.

callbacks.explanation: Endgame gives the 2012 Loki a second chance at the cube and lets him escape. That version of Loki is the one picked up later in the Loki TV series (2021).

callbacks.title: The Trip Through the Wormhole

foreshadow.scene: End of the Battle of New York
foreshadow.description: Tony grabs the nuclear missile fired at Manhattan and flies it through the wormhole in what looks like a one-way trip. The Hulk catches him as he falls back.

fulfillment.description: Tony takes the Stones and uses them against Thanos and his army, and this time the sacrifice costs him his life.

callbacks.explanation: The Avengers shows Tony willing to die for everyone else. Endgame finishes the act he survived the first time.

callbacks.title: The Killian Plot

foreshadow.description: At a New Year's Eve party in 1999, Aldrich Killian, then disabled, asks Tony to join his company A.I.M., and Tony brushes him off.

fulfillment.description: Thirteen years later, Killian turns out to be the mastermind behind the Mandarin attacks, after using Extremis to cure his own disability.

callbacks.explanation: One careless brush-off in 1999 becomes the villain's whole reason for the plot.

callbacks.title: Extremis Has a Flaw

foreshadow.description: Tony finds out the "Mandarin bombings" were really soldiers on Extremis whose bodies rejected it and exploded, covered up to hide the treatment's flaws.

fulfillment.description: Pepper, injected with Extremis by Killian, survives a deadly fall because of it and kills Killian. Afterwards Tony helps stabilize the Extremis in her.

callbacks.explanation: The flaw that makes Extremis a weapon is the danger hanging over Pepper. The film ends with Tony fixing it for her rather than for Killian.

callbacks.title: Tony's Panic Attacks

foreshadow.scene: End of the Battle of New York
foreshadow.description: Tony flies through the wormhole into space, sees the alien fleet and blacks out before falling back to Earth.

fulfillment.description: Months later Tony has post-traumatic stress, panic attacks and insomnia from the invasion, and copes by building dozens of suits.

callbacks.explanation: Iron Man 3 treats the climax of The Avengers as something Tony has not got over, and builds his story around it.

callbacks.title: The Mandarin Is an Actor

foreshadow.description: A terrorist called the Mandarin claims a series of bombings in videos broadcast around the world.

fulfillment.description: Tony finds that the Mandarin is Trevor Slattery, an English actor hired by Killian and A.I.M. to play the part and cover up the Extremis explosions.

callbacks.explanation: The terrorist in the broadcasts is a performance, and the real villain is the businessman behind it.

callbacks.title: Pepper Ends the Fight

foreshadow.scene: Final fight on the Stark Industries roof
foreshadow.description: Outmatched by Stane, Tony tells Pepper to overload the building's big arc reactor. The surge sends Stane falling into it and kills him.

fulfillment.description: With Tony cornered by Killian, Pepper, now with Extremis powers, attacks Killian and kills him.

callbacks.explanation: In both films Tony cannot finish the main villain himself and Pepper does. In Iron Man 3 she does it in the fight herself.

callbacks.title: Cap, Out of Time

foreshadow.description: After nearly 70 years frozen in ice (shown at the end of Captain America: The First Avenger), Steve is still adjusting to a world where most people he knew are gone when Fury brings him in.

fulfillment.description: After returning the Stones, Steve stays in the past and lives his life with Peggy Carter. He comes back an old man and passes his shield to Sam Wilson.

callbacks.explanation: The man out of time finally goes back to his own time and gets the life he lost.

callbacks.title: Thanos's Threat

foreshadow.description: The Other reports the failed attack on Earth to his master. The film does not name him; Kevin Feige confirmed it was Thanos.

fulfillment.description: Thor kills the present-day Thanos early in the film. A 2014 Thanos then follows the Avengers to the present and is wiped out by Tony in the final battle.

callbacks.explanation: Thanos was teased in a few seconds in 2012 and was not defeated until 2019.

callbacks.title: Back to the Battle of New York

foreshadow.description: The Chitauri pour through a portal over Stark Tower and the six Avengers fight them across Manhattan.

fulfillment.description: Bruce, Scott, Steve and Tony travel back to New York in 2012, during Loki's attack, to steal the Space, Mind and Time Stones from that day.

callbacks.explanation: Endgame walks back into the 2012 battle, with the 2012 versions of the heroes still in the scene.

callbacks.title: Coulson Meets His Hero

foreshadow.description: Coulson, who grew up idolizing Captain America, finally meets Steve Rogers.

fulfillment.description: Loki kills Coulson with the scepter, and Fury uses Coulson's death to get the divided heroes to fight as one team.

callbacks.explanation: Making Coulson the team's biggest fan makes his death hit harder, and it is what brings the group together.

callbacks.title: Infinity Stone: Space

foreshadow.description: The Tesseract is described as a powerful energy source of unknown potential. The film never calls it an Infinity Stone; Kevin Feige later said it holds the Space Stone.

fulfillment.description: The Space Stone goes into the Nano Gauntlet Tony builds, and Bruce uses the gauntlet to bring back everyone Thanos erased.

callbacks.explanation: The glowing cube that drives the first team-up is part of the tool that undoes the Blip.

callbacks.title: Infinity Stone: Mind

foreshadow.description: Loki uses his scepter to take control of Erik Selvig and Clint Barton. The film does not say what powers it; Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015) shows the Mind Stone inside.

fulfillment.scene: The time heist at Stark Tower
fulfillment.description: Steve takes the 2012 scepter, with the Mind Stone in it, from Hydra sleeper agents inside S.H.I.E.L.D., and later uses it to knock out his 2012 self.

callbacks.explanation: The mind-control weapon from 2012 becomes one of the six Stones the team needs.

callbacks.title: Banner and the Stones

foreshadow.description: S.H.I.E.L.D. brings Bruce in because his gamma radiation expertise can track the Tesseract.

fulfillment.description: Bruce, now merged with the Hulk, wears the Nano Gauntlet with all six Stones and brings back everyone lost in the Blip.

callbacks.explanation: The scientist hired to track one Stone ends up being the one who uses all six of them to save people.

callbacks.title: Avengers... Assemble

foreshadow.description: The team forms, but nobody says the comics' rallying cry "Avengers assemble". Kevin Feige felt it did not fit the film, and Age of Ultron (2015) cut Cap off mid-line.

fulfillment.description: With every returned hero gathered behind him, Steve finally says "Avengers... assemble" before the charge against Thanos's army.

callbacks.explanation: Marvel held the comics' most famous line back for seven years and used it once the full team was assembled.

callbacks.title: From Scraps to the Nano Gauntlet

foreshadow.description: Held captive, Tony and Yinsen build a small arc reactor and the first armored suit out of the weapons parts around them.

fulfillment.scene: The time heist and final battle
fulfillment.description: Tony works out time travel, helps build the Nano Gauntlet that holds the six Stones, and in the end moves the Stones into his own armor.

callbacks.explanation: Tony's story starts and ends with him building his way out of a situation nobody else can get out of.

callbacks.title: The Team Assembles

foreshadow.description: After fighting each other on the Helicarrier, six heroes fight together for the first time against Loki's invasion.

fulfillment.description: Sorcerers' portals open and the returned heroes, the Guardians, the Ravagers and the armies of Wakanda and Asgard arrive to face Thanos.

callbacks.explanation: The first team-up is six heroes. Endgame's assembly brings in almost everyone the MCU had introduced by then.

callbacks.title: "And I Am Iron Man"

foreshadow.description: Tony ends the first film by telling the world "I am Iron Man."

fulfillment.description: In the final battle Tony takes the Stones from Thanos, says "I am Iron Man" and snaps his fingers.

callbacks.explanation: Tony's first and last big lines are the same words. The Endgame line was not in the original script; it was added in post-production and shot in reshoots.

source.name: Screen Rant: Avengers: Endgame Crowd Shocked By Tony Stark's I Am Iron Man Scene
